english.title: Enter United Kingdom lawfully without leave but remain beyond time limit
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), not being a British Citizen and having lawfully entered the United Kingdom without leave by virtue of section 8(1) of the Immigration Act 1971, remained without leave beyond the time allowed by section 8(1)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 24(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1971.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 28 applies and extends the time limit for prosecution.
(ii) Section 8 allows the crew of ships or aircraft to enter without leave for up to seven days.

other.powersofarrest: Arrest without warrantBy section 28A of the Immigration Act 1971 (as amended by the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999) an immigration official may arrest without warrant a person who has committed or attempted to commit an offence under section 24 or section 24A of the Immigration Act 1971.
other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
36 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
